Hi Arielle — thanks for the clear list and the doc. Attaching a concise export spec (redwood_audit_export_spec_v1.pdf) and a small sample (sample-export.jsonl) that demonstrates the payload shape. High-level answers inline below; happy to go deeper on a call.

1) Formats: Redwood supports JSONL/NDJSON and compressed Parquet for bulk exports. For forensic exports we typically default to NDJSON with accompanying manifest metadata.

2) Max export window: Customers with Dedicated or Private deployments can request exports covering their entire retention window. For Hosted accounts we retain audit trails for up to the configured retention tier (default 90 days, configurable up to 7 years for enterprise contracts). One-off extracts can include the full retained history.

3) Integrity & tamper evidence: Exports include a signed manifest with per-file SHA256 checksums and a manifest signature using the customer's KMS-wrapped key (enterprise only). We also include event sequencing metadata and monotonic timestamps to support chain-of-custody.

4) Time-to-deliver SLA: We offer a target of 72 hours for standard bulk export requests under enterprise SLAs; expedited forensics (on-call) is available under a premium response SLA (contracted). We can put specific time windows into the MOP in the contract.

5) Retention tiers: Audit trails and platform telemetry are independently configurable. Default retention tiers are: 90 days (standard), 2 years (extended), 7 years (archival/enterprise). Retention deletion is policy-driven and we provide programmatic snapshots prior to deletion for legal hold.

Next steps: I propose a short technical walkthrough with Ben (solutions engineering) and Jonas (legal/controls liaison) to confirm manifest formats and the contractual language for SLAs. Proposed times: Mon 10 May 09:00-10:00 PT or Tue 11 May 14:00-15:00 PT. Which works?

Thanks,

Arielle — adding a few technical clarifications so procurement can see specifics they requested.

- Export sharding & performance: Large exports are generated as sharded NDJSON files (default 1GB shards) and delivered to a pre-authorized S3 bucket or via secure transfer. We can tune shard size for faster parallel ingest on your side.

- Schema & ordering: Each event record includes an immutable event_id, source_service, iso8601 timestamp, sequence_id (within shard) and an operation_hash. The sample-export.jsonl shows the exact keys. We also provide a lightweight index file to speed queries.

- Immutable snapshot mode: For Private deployments we can generate a notarized snapshot with an HSM-backed signature; for Hosted we provide SHA256 manifests signed by our KMS (with export traceability metadata). Both options include a chain-of-custody CSV that lists the export job steps.

- Redaction options: We support configurable redaction rules (regex or schema-driven) applied at export time and provide an unredacted forensic channel under customer-managed access controls for legal holds.

- Delivery SLA examples: Standard bulk: 72 hours; High-priority forensic (on-call): 8 hours (subject to pact). We'll enumerate exact SLAs in the mutual-action-plan.

If helpful, I can share a brief demo script for your engineering team to validate sample-import performance.

Ben Carter
